solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Drink tea perhaps, maintaining sober condition at first (6)

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the meal holds the other letters inside it
'at first' points at the opening letter of each of the words before it

blocks.note: tea is a meal, especially an early evening one; 'perhaps' flags an example
first letters of Sober Condition, held inside ME…AL

annotation.surface: Someone swaps the drink for tea, keeping sober at the start of the evening.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drink tea' reads as one action, but 'Drink' is the definition and 'tea' is a meal, as in the British evening meal called tea.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: it is a Mexican spirit distilled from agave.

entries.clue: Artist and author’s personal pronouns — start to finish (6)

indicators.note: the start is sent to the finish: the first letter moves to the end

blocks.note: the author calls themself ME and what they own MINE

annotation.surface: A grammar note about the pronouns a writer uses of themself.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter is the author, so the author's pronouns are the first-person ME and MINE. Eminem is the American rapper, a recording artist.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the rapper is a best-selling recording artist.

entries.clue: Smart person using pivoted device to split two hundred timber pieces (6,5)

indicators.note: to split something is to come between its parts, so the device goes between the two Cs

blocks.note: two Roman hundreds, C and C
a lever turns on a pivot; it sits between the Cs
logs are pieces of timber

annotation.surface: A craftsman levering apart lengths of wood.
annotation.walkthrough: CLEVER CLOGS is British slang, usually mocking, for a know-all.
annotation.definitionFit: British idiom: a jokey, slightly mocking name for someone smart or too pleased with being smart.

entries.clue: Top of leg cramped, not initially eased (9)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the top of a word is its first letter
'initially' points at the first letter, and 'not' drops it from TIGHTENED

blocks.note: first letter of Leg
TIGHTENED (cramped) without its T

annotation.surface: A muscle cramp high in the leg that slowly eases.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top of leg' looks like the thigh, but it only means the letter L.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: taking weight off a burden or worry makes it easier.

entries.clue: Story books editor gifted (8)

blocks.note: a tale is a story
NT = New Testament, a set of books
the usual abbreviation

annotation.surface: A publisher's praise for a story editor.
annotation.walkthrough: NT, the New Testament, is the standard crossword stand-in for 'books'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone with natural ability.

entries.clue: Later on drunk eats (7)

indicators.note: what eats takes something inside it, so TIGHT takes in ON

blocks.note: tight = drunk, informally; it goes round ON
used as itself, inside T…IGHT

annotation.surface: Someone who has had too much to drink finally eats something later on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Later on' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Later' and 'on' is the word swallowed by TIGHT.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: this evening is later on today, and both work as adverbs of time.

entries.clue: Lady in caravan rolled up (5)

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow
in a down clue, going up means reading the letters backwards

blocks.note: the letters straddle the join of caravAN and ROLled; 'up' flips them

annotation.surface: A woman sits in a caravan with the awning rolled up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rolled up' pretends to describe the caravan, but 'up' tells a down clue to read backwards, while 'rolled' only donates letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: it is a woman's name, as in the novel Lorna Doone.

entries.clue: Pinch small amount of alcohol (3)

blocks.note: to squeeze skin between finger and thumb
a small measure of spirits, a dram

annotation.surface: Stealing a drop of drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pinch' reads as steal, but here it is a squeeze between the fingers.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: a sharp squeeze, and a small measure of whisky or brandy.

entries.clue: Staying close with university group (8)

blocks.note: the close of something is its end
the usual abbreviation
a ring is a group, as of plotters

annotation.surface: Keeping in touch with a university society.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close' reads as near, but it is the noun: an end.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe something that lasts rather than fading.

entries.clue: Bravo leaving Edinburgh after assassination? (5,3)

indicators.note: what leaves a word goes out of it, so B quits EDINBURGH
an assassination does violence, and the remaining letters are violently mangled

blocks.note: B in the NATO alphabet; it leaves EDINBURGH
EDINBURGH less B, then rearranged

annotation.surface: A hit man slips out of Edinburgh after a killing.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a paid killer would indeed leave the city after the hit. A bravo is also an old word for a hired assassin.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: read straight, the clue describes a paid killer fleeing the scene of the job.

entries.clue: Dangerous section of river primarily perilous in storms (6)

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take the first letter
that letter goes inside the next word

blocks.note: to storm a place is to raid it; RAIDS goes round P
first letter of Perilous

annotation.surface: A warning that one stretch of river turns perilous in bad weather.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Storms' reads as weather, but it is attacks: raids.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: the fast, turbulent, rock-strewn stretch of a river.

entries.clue: Concerned about fellow ruler (6)

blocks.note: re = concerning, as in memo headers
a gent is a fellow

annotation.surface: Worrying about someone who is in charge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Concerned about' reads as worried, but it is RE, meaning on the subject of.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one who rules in place of a monarch who is absent or too young.

entries.clue: Merganser actively shunning northern lake (8)

indicators.note: the letters are active, moving around
to shun is to avoid, so the N is left out

blocks.note: the fodder
the usual abbreviation; it is removed

annotation.surface: A diving duck avoiding a lake up north.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Northern lake' reads together, but 'northern' is the N that leaves. Grasmere is a lake in England's Lake District.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a small lake in Cumbria, in northern England.

entries.clue: A lot remains to be resolved about brothers (11)

indicators.note: to resolve is to break down and rework, so the letters are to be worked out afresh

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: Much is still to be settled concerning some siblings.
annotation.walkthrough: The brothers are monks, not siblings, so 'about brothers' is the adjective: relating to monks.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-flavoured sense: monks are brothers, and this adjective relates to monks and their houses.

entries.clue: Checking drawbacks connected with exercise (12)

blocks.note: pros and cons: the cons are the drawbacks
training is exercise

annotation.surface: Weighing up the disadvantages of a workout.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Checking' reads as looking over, but it means holding back.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to check something is to restrain or hold it back.

entries.clue: Pack beneath post somewhere on ship (9)

indicators.note: in a down clue, what is beneath comes lower, so DECK follows AFTER

blocks.note: post as in post-war: after
a pack of cards is a deck

annotation.surface: Stowing a pack under a post on board.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like a pole or mail, but it is the prefix meaning after.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the open deck towards the stern is one place on a ship.

entries.clue: Have machines take over from assistant beneath car (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, what is beneath comes lower, so MATE follows AUTO

blocks.note: an auto is a car
a mate is an assistant, as a plumber's mate

annotation.surface: Machines replace the mechanic's helper working under the car.
annotation.walkthrough: A plumber's mate is a British term for a tradesman's helper, which is why MATE means assistant.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain paraphrase: the verb means handing a job over to machines.

entries.clue: Maybe servants baron studies suspiciously (12)

indicators.note: something suspicious is not straight, so the letters are out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: A baron eyes his household staff with suspicion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks servants as one example of the wider class.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: servants are one kind of people ranking below others.

entries.clue: Square leg is one often hit by ball (7)

blocks.note: nine is a square number, three times three
pins is slang for legs

annotation.surface: A cricket fielder at square leg is often struck by the ball.
annotation.walkthrough: Square leg is a fielding position in cricket, but the cricket is a decoy: the phrase splits in two, and the ball in the definition belongs to skittles.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a skittle is knocked down by the bowled ball, often.

entries.clue: Greatly admire the other side having lost final to rivals (6)

indicators.note: what has been lost is gone, so a letter is removed
the final of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: the reverse is the other side of a coin
last letter of rivalS; REVERSE loses it

annotation.surface: A fan still admires the opposing team after they lose a final to their rivals.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is sport, but 'the other side' is the reverse of a coin, and the lost final is a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to hold someone in deep respect.

entries.clue: Revolt reported on much of central part of island (8)

indicators.note: much but not all, so the last letter goes
what is reported is heard, so the word is given by its sound
in an across clue, what is on something comes after it

blocks.note: CORE, the central part, less its last letter
to revolt someone is to sicken them

annotation.surface: News of a rebellion in the heart of an island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolt' reads as uprising, the right idea for Corsica's history, but it is the verb: to disgust.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective from a place name: belonging to Corsica, the Mediterranean island.

entries.clue: Pick cosmetic product (5)

blocks.note: the best of a group, as in 'the pick of the bunch'
something smoothed onto the skin

annotation.surface: Choosing something to put on your face.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pick' reads as a verb, but it is the noun: the best.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: the best part of anything, and a lotion for the skin.

entries.clue: Feel me regularly probing inflamed wound (6)

indicators.note: 'regularly' means at regular intervals, so every second letter is taken
a probe pushes inside, so the letters go into the next word

blocks.note: inflamed skin is red; RE…D goes round ELE
fEeL mE

annotation.surface: Someone asks you to feel as they probe a sore, inflamed injury.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wound' reads as an injury, but it is the past of wind, as a fishing line is wound in.
annotation.definitionFit: A different sense of the word: wound rhymes with sound here, the past tense of wind, as thread onto a spool.

entries.clue: Speculation of mould’s origin in wall section (6)

indicators.note: a word's origin is where it begins, so its first letter
that letter goes inside the next words

blocks.note: a gable is the triangular section of wall under a pitched roof; it goes round M
first letter of Mould

annotation.surface: Guessing where the mould in a wall came from.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Speculation' reads as guessing, but it is a risky venture.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a speculation is a risky bet on an uncertain outcome.

entries.clue: Strip naked, almost entirely (3)

indicators.note: almost the whole word: everything except its last letter

blocks.note: BARE less its final E

annotation.surface: Undressing until almost nothing is left on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Strip' reads as undress, but it is the noun, as in a strip of metal or chocolate.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a long narrow piece of metal or chocolate.

entries.clue: Pledges to leave old in favour of new unclad property (8)

indicators.note: to leave is to go away, so the O departs from PROMISES
one thing dropped in favour of another is replaced by it
unclad means stripped, so the outer letters come off

blocks.note: a pledge is a promise
the usual abbreviation; it leaves
nEw stripped of its outer letters; it replaces the O

annotation.surface: Vows to swap an old place for a new bare one.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unclad property' reads as a bare house, but 'unclad' only strips the word 'new'.
annotation.definitionFit: Estate-agent and legal usage: a building together with its land.

entries.clue: Worker on crossing oiled nut according to Spooner (8)

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the M and F change places

blocks.note: oiled and merry are both slang for tipsy; the M swaps for an F
a nut is an enthusiast, a fan; the F swaps for an M

annotation.surface: A worker on a railway crossing oils a nut.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crossing' suggests a road or railway, but it is a crossing of water, and 'oiled nut' is a drunk fan.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: the one who works a boat across a river or strait.

entries.clue: Taxing task poorly tackled by king and queen (6)

indicators.note: a tackler grips a player, so the outer letters grip the word

blocks.note: chess abbreviation
poorly = unwell
ER = Elizabeth Regina

annotation.surface: A royal couple take on a tough job badly.
annotation.walkthrough: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the standard crossword queen.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal usage: anything brutally hard, a job or an exam, gets this murderous label.
